translations.text: In the tenth year of King Khosrow, while Arvand Gushnasp was marzpan of Kartli, a man came from Persia,
from the land of Arshaketi, the son of a magus. He was a pagan, his name was Gvirobandak, and in age he was a young man of about thirty years.
He came to the city of Mtskheta and was learning the craft of shoemaking.
There he saw the law of the Christians, the worship of Christ, and the power of the Holy Cross made manifest.
He came to love the law of Christianity and believed in Christ. When he had learned shoemaking, he asked for a Christian wife, became a Christian himself, and received baptism.
At his baptism they gave him the name Eustathius. Holy Eustathius lived in Christianity and in the virtue of Christ.
At that time the Persians who were in Mtskheta, the sorcerers and the shoemakers, gathered together and were celebrating a feast.
They sent for the blessed Eustathius and said to him: "Come and join us in this festivity of ours."
But the blessed Eustathius laughed at them and said to them: "Your feast is darkness, and you who celebrate it are darkness too,
but I have received the seal of Christ and I celebrate the feast of Christ, for I am sealed with the seal of Christ and am separated from that darkness of yours."
When they had finished the feast, those same sorcerers and shoemakers gathered and took counsel before Ustam, the commander of the fortress of Mtskheta, and said:
"There is a man here from our religion who does not come to the feast with us and does not kindle fire; he even blasphemes our religion and insults us, and says, 'I am a Christian.'
Now summon him and question him, for you hold authority in this city."

Ustam, the commander of the fortress of Mtskheta, listened to what they said about Eustathius and sent one of the horsemen to summon the blessed Eustathius, who said to him angrily: "The commander orders you to come."
But holy Eustathius faltered a little and wanted to hold back. And then [?] he thought it over and said:
"These are my companions. If I am afraid even of them, how will I stand before the great princes later?!"
No, I will go to him and openly confess Christ, for I have heard from the holy Gospel what he said:
'Whoever confesses me before men, I too will confess before my Father in heaven; and whoever denies me before men,
I too will deny before my Father who is in heaven.'" He made the sign of the cross on his forehead and his heart and said: "The Lord is with me."
And the blessed Eustathius came and stood before Ustam, the commander of the fortress of Mtskheta. And the man who had summoned him said to Ustam:
"This is a man who insults our religion." And the fortress commander looked at the blessed Eustathius and said:
"I am speaking to you, man: tell me, what land are you from, or what city, and what religion do you hold?"
Holy Eustathius said to him: "I was from the land of Persia, from the district of Arshaketi; I was from the city of Gandzak.

My father was a magus and taught me the religion of the magi too, but I did not take up the religion of the magi, for in the city of Gandzak most people are Christians, and there are a bishop and priests,
and through them I was drawn on beyond everything else, for Christianity is greater than every religion, greater than godlessness.
And now I believe in Christ and I am in the service of Christ."
But Ustam, the commander of the fortress, said to him: "No one will allow you to be a servant of Christ, and if you do not give up this madness peacefully, great torment will come upon you."
But Saint Eustathius said to him: "I am prepared not only for torment for the love of Christ, but I do not spare myself even unto death."
When Ustam saw the earnest steadfastness of the blessed Eustathius, he considered and said:
"I have no authority to punish this man at all, neither to bind him to a stake nor to imprison him; rather, I will send him to the city of Tbilisi, to Arvand Gushnasp,
the marzpan of Kartli, and let him do whatever seems fitting to him, for he has authority over the death and life of every person in Kartli."
And Ustam, the commander of the fortress of Mtskheta, ordered two horsemen to take the blessed Eustathius to Tbilisi.
And those same sorcerers and enchanters gathered together and came to Ustam and said to him:
"There are others here as well of our religion, and they too are Christians; order them also to be summoned and to be taken to Tbilisi as well."
But Ustam said to them: "Who are they?" And they told him their names and said to him:
"One is called Gushnak, and one Bakhdiad, one Burzo, one Panagushnasp, one Perozak, one Zarmil, one Stephen."

And Ustam ordered them to be summoned. But he held no trial of them at all; he only ordered all eight of them to be bound and handed over [and sent] to Tbilisi, to Arvand Gushnasp, the marzpan of Kartli, and he sent word to him thus:
"These men were of our religion and have taken up the religion of the Christians; I have seized them and sent them to you, my lord, for you have authority to judge them."
And they brought all eight of them before the marzpan, and he said to them: "Who are you, and what religion do you hold?"
And they told him, each man his own district and each one's village, and they all said to him:
"We were in our ancestral religion and followed the religion of the Persians; but when we came into Kartli and saw the religion of the Christians, we became Christians, and now we are Christians,
for the religion of the Christians is holy and fragrant and is exceedingly good and beautiful, and no other religion can equal the religion of the Christians."
Now the one who answered the judge on their behalf was the blessed Eustathius.
And when he heard such words from them, he grew angry in his heart and ordered his servants to strike the blessed ones in the face and to take them all outside, and he ordered:
"Shave their heads and beards, pierce their noses, put chains on their necks and fetters on their feet,
and put them in prison; and if any of them professes the ancestral religion, release him and bring him to me, and I will enrich him with a great gift.
"But whoever does not profess the religion of his fathers must die in prison." And when they heard the marzban's words:
"Whoever professes it, I will let him live, and whoever does not profess the religion of his fathers must die in prison,"
at that moment the devil entered the hearts of Bakhdiad and Panagushnasp, and they denied Christ and professed godlessness, and they received their portion with the crucifiers.
But the blessed Eustathius and Gushnak and Borzo and Perozak and Zarmil and Stephen stood earnestly and firmly in the faith of Christ,
When the marzban was told that two of them had professed their ancestral religion,
the marzban was glad. He ordered them brought in, had them seated [?], and promised them great wealth and good treatment.
But as for the blessed Eustathius and his other companions, he ordered that their heads and beards be shaved, that chains be put on their necks, and that they be thrown into prison in fetters.
The servants carried out the marzban's order. They shaved their hair and beards and put them in prison, bound in chains.
He comforted Bakhdiad and Panagushnasp and let them go. But of the wealth and good things he had promised them, he did not give them even a single psiridi [?a small coin].
They kept Saint Eustathius and his other companions in prison for only about six months.
After six months a summoner from the king of the Persians came for Arvand Gushnasp.
As the marzban was setting out to go to the king, the princes of Kartli gathered and came to take leave of the marzban.

When the marzban was mounting his horse, the princes of Kartli rose up: Samuel, Catholicos of Kartli; Gregory, steward (mamasakhlisi) of Kartli; Arshusha, pitiakhsh (viceroy) of Kartli; and the other princes of the royal house. They said to the marzban:
"We beg your lordship; we ask you for one favour." And he said to them: "Speak, whatever you wish!
What could there be that I would not grant you?" And all of them said to him:
"We beg you, lord, may it please you to release those men of Mtskheta who have been put in prison for Christianity."
The marzban said to them, "Those men were meant to be put to death, but at your intercession I release them." And they thanked him.
He ordered their release. They brought them out of the prison, and they went to their own homes as Christians.
Those blessed men lived in a way pleasing to God. By God's will some of them have died over the course of time, and some are still alive.
But of those who denied Christ, Bakhdiad became possessed by a demon and died a hard death, and the wretched Panagushnasp spent his days in poverty.
He had no bread to eat and could find no clothing to cover his body, and as long as he lived his days were spent in sorrow and hardship.
Three years later Vezhan Buzmir came in as marzban of Kartli.
The Persians of Mtskheta who had accused the blessed Eustathius went to Tbilisi, stood before the marzban Vezhan Buzmir, and said to him:
"There are men in Mtskheta of our religion who have fallen away from us and practise Christianity. Now it is in your power to judge them."
Vezhan Buzmir ordered two horsemen to go and summon Saint Eustathius and Stephen.
When the horsemen arrived, they said to Eustathius and Stephen, "The marzban summons you." And they replied, "We will come with you. We are not troubled, nor are we afraid."
As Eustathius and Stephen were setting out for Tbilisi, Eustathius said to his mother-in-law, his wife, his children, and his servants and maidservants:
"Farewell to you, for I will not come back here again. I will not deny Christ, and they will not let me go alive.
My death will take place in prison in Tbilisi, and my head will be cut off, but by God's will my body will be brought back here." When he had said this to them, he took leave of them all.
And all of them made the sign of the cross, and he and Stephen set out for Tbilisi with the horsemen, while their households, kinsmen and their own people followed behind them weeping.
And when they had gone out into the plain and come before the Cross of Mtskheta, Saint Eustathius raised his hands and said:
"Lord God, Jesus Christ, if you count me worthy of death for your name as a Christian, do not let my body be thrown outside and eaten by dogs and by the birds of the sky,
but command that my body be brought back here and buried in Mtskheta, where I received baptism."
When blessed Eustathius had said these words, he bowed down before the Cross and parted from the gathering, and they set out for Tbilisi.
And when the horsemen arrived, they brought Eustathius and Stephen before the marzban Vezhan Buzmir and said:
"These are the new Christians from Mtskheta." And Vezhan Buzmir said to Eustathius and Stephen:
"Who are you, and what religion do you hold?" And the leading men of the Assyrians stood up on behalf of Stephen and said to him:
"We know this man; he is our fellow townsman. His father and mother and brothers and sisters are Christians, and he too is a Christian."
And on their word they released Stephen. But to Saint Eustathius he said: "Where are you from, and by what religion do you live?"
Saint Eustathius said: "If you ask me, listen carefully and I will tell you everything.
I was from the land of Persia, from the district of Arshaketi, from the city of Gandzak. My father was a magus and my brothers were magi, and my father was also teaching me the magian religion.

But I did not love my ancestral religion, and I said in my mind: I do not love this religion; now I will listen to that of the Jews and also to that of the Christians, and whichever is better, that religion I will come to love.
And by day my father would teach me the magian religion, and at night, when the Christians rang for the service,
I would go to the church and listen to their office, and I would watch the worship that the Christians performed for God.
And I also went into the synagogue with the Jews and watched their worship too.
But at the prayer of the Christians their voice sounded to me like the voice of an angel, and their office is very fragrant and sweet.
But when I went into the Jews' synagogue at night, I could understand nothing of what they were saying.
And afterwards I went in again, and Samuel the archdeacon, who was learned in the law, came up to me and said to me: Why have you come into the church so eagerly?
And I said to him: Lord, you also know who I am; but I do not love this ancestral religion of mine, and I wish
that someone would teach me both the religion of the Jews and that of the Christians, and whichever religion is holier, that one I would come to love.
"Then Samuel the archdeacon said to me: If you truly wish to know, I will explain both religions to you well.
But the choosing is not yours; rather, it is as the Lord commands you.
And I begged him earnestly and said to him: The religion by which I may be pleasing to God is the religion I wish to hold; command that one to me as well.
[845] Then Samuel the archdeacon began to explain and said to me: Listen carefully, brother!
In earlier times there was the religion of the Persians, as you yourself know; but God hated that religion of the Persians and was not pleased with it.
And then God chose the Jews and was pleased with them, and he gave them the law and the commandment to keep.
Only then did God become more pleased with the Christians than with the Jews.
And then I begged Samuel the archdeacon and said to him: "Lord, do not be annoyed with me, and explain it to me properly."
And then I asked: "Lord, who were the Jews? Where did they come from, and how did God come to love them?" Then Samuel the archdeacon said to me:
"The story of the Jews is a long one, brother. But if you open your ears and listen carefully, I will gladly tell you all of it and make it known to you.
"There was a man, blameless and God-loving, in the land of the Persians, in the city of the Babylonians, and his name was Abraham.
And God appeared to him in a vision of the night and said to Abraham:
'Go out from that land of yours, and I will lead you to another land. I will multiply you and increase you very greatly, and I will make you the father of many nations and of countless peoples.'
And Abraham believed that word of God, and Abraham said: 'Let that word of yours come to pass for me, Lord!'
And Abraham went out from the land of the Chaldeans and came to the land between the rivers, to the city of Canaan, near the Euphrates.
He came under the guidance of an angel and settled in Canaan.
And then he moved him from there and brought him to the land of Canaan, and he settled in Hebron.
And a son, Isaac, was born to Abraham, and to Isaac, Jacob. And Jacob had twelve sons. And God commanded Abraham and said to him:
'Circumcise Isaac and Jacob and all the sons of Jacob, and let this be a law for you forever.'
"And Abraham did as God had commanded him. And the descendants of Abraham increased and multiplied very greatly. These are the Jews.
And God loved the Jews very greatly, as a father loves a beloved child. And he gave the Jews the name Israel.
Now 'Israel' is interpreted as 'people of God.' And that people of God, Israel, grew great and spread out,
and God came down from heaven to earth and came onto the summit of Mount Sinai. And with his own hand God wrote the law and the commandment on tablets of stone, as follows:
"The first commandment is this: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.
And then this: Do not kill, do not steal, do not commit fornication, do not desire your neighbour's wife, do not swear falsely, do not bear false witness, do not be double-tongued.
Honour your father and your mother. Love your neighbour as yourself. Keep my sabbaths. Observe the feasts, the offerings and the days of rest.
God wrote this law and commandment and gave it to Moses, his servant. And Moses took those tablets and read them aloud to all Israel.
And all Israel rejoiced and said: 'Everything the Lord has commanded us we will do and carry out, only let the Lord be with us.' And the Lord went up into heaven.
And when the Jews had heard this law, they made offerings and burned incense and offered sacrifices, and they kept the sabbaths, and God was with them.
And at that time foreigners gathered and attacked Israel. But God drove them away by the hand of one man.
Some of them they killed, some they brought back as captives, and some they put to flight. So they no longer had to fear their enemies, for God was with them.
"Some time later, all Israel asked God for a king who would fight their enemies.
God commanded that they have a king, and God established the order of royal majesty.
Some days later that king was killed in battle, because he had exalted himself and trusted in his own strength and not in his God.
"After him David reigned. David was beloved of God, and God loved David. David fulfilled the consecrated offerings [?], the oblations and the sacrifices, and he kept the feasts and the sabbaths well.
After him his son Solomon reigned. He turned away from God, and the people turned away and departed from God and served deaf idols,
idols made by hands, and lifeless stones, trees, high hills and the tops of trees, and they denied God.
The prophets cried out and said to them: "It is not right to abandon the living God and to serve stones or anything else.
Now behold, God will send death, famine, sword and captivity upon you, and so he will wipe you out."
But they did not want to hear the voice of their prophets, for the people of Israel had become frenzied.
They ordered those prophets to be slaughtered: some by the sword, some by fire,
some they sawed apart with a saw, some they gave to wild beasts, some they threw into a pit, and some they stoned to death.
"But God is gentle and loves humankind. He did not want Israel to be destroyed; he wanted them to turn back to him.
God sent his Son Christ into the world. He entered the womb of the holy Virgin, put on flesh and became man from holy Mary. He came forth from the holy womb and covered his divinity with flesh.

If he had not covered his divinity with flesh, no human being could have approached God. For the sun is a creation of God, yet no one can fix his eyes on it, and no one can gaze at the disk of the sun.
No human being could have approached the divinity. Therefore he put on flesh, so that he might somehow turn Israel back to the living God.
After he became man, he was baptized in the river Jordan by the hand of John.
As he came up out of the water, behold, the heavens opened, and the Holy Spirit came down, white like a dove, and rested upon him. A voice came down from heaven and said:
"This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him and you will live."
"When he entered Jerusalem, he began to perform miracles, signs and healings.
A man who had been sick for thirty-eight years lay on a bed. He saw him and commanded with a word: "Rise, take up your bed and walk!"
At once the man rose and walked, alive, and glorified God.
"Then he found a man blind from birth. He made clay with his spittle, smeared it on the man's eyes and told him to wash with water, and the eyes of the blind man were opened.
He raised the dead, made the lame walk and cleansed lepers, and Christ performed many healings among them,
so that the Jews might believe and turn back to the living God. He wanted them not to be rejected by God,
But the Jews became all the more enraged, and they conceived great envy against Christ and wanted to kill him.
But Christ withdrew from them to the outlying villages and hamlets, and he stayed there.
And those who believed in Christ followed after him. And he was going out to a certain village, and a dead man was being carried out, [?] (iamavri), the son of a widow.
And when he saw it, he gave a command, and they set down the bier. And he took the boy by the hand and gave him back alive to his mother.

Then he was going out to a certain village, and a great crowd followed him. Because of the size of the crowd they could not bring the paralytic [?] into his presence, so they stripped off the roof of the house and let him down from there on a bed.
And he raised him up, and he went to his house on his own feet. And a great crowd followed him and glorified God.
And from among the people he chose twelve men and called them disciples, and whatever he commanded them, that they did.
And he entered a certain village. There was a wedding there. And Jesus went into the wedding house, and there was no wine there, because it had run out, and empty jars stood there.
Then Jesus commanded the disciples to bring water, and they filled the jars with water, and Christ blessed that water.
And it became wine better than the first wine, and many marveled, and they believed in him and followed him.
And next, there was a woman who had been in a flow of blood for twelve years. She came secretly up behind Jesus and grasped the hem of his garment, and she was cleansed.
And next, Christ was coming to a certain place, and there was a beautiful field there. He looked at the crowd that was following after him and said to the disciples:
"This crowd has gone so many days without food, and I have pity on them. Go to the city and buy bread and give it to the crowd."
But Christ said to the disciples: "Does none of you have any bread here?"
And one of the disciples said to him: "I have five loaves and two fish." Christ said: "Bring them here to me."
And when they brought the five loaves and the two fish, Christ commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground, and he lifted up the five loaves and the two fish toward heaven,
blessed them and broke them and gave them to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
And the crowd ate and was satisfied, and they took up twelve full baskets of leftovers.
And the people who ate numbered about five thousand, not counting children and women.
Then Christ commanded the crowd to go by dry land.
But Christ and his disciples crossed the sea as if on dry land, and their feet did not get wet.
And when they came out onto dry land, a man met them who had in him a demon, Legion.
He cried out and said: "Christ, help me, for I am cruelly tormented!" And Christ rebuked the demon Legion, and it went out of him, and he glorified God.
But the demon cried out and said: "Christ, I know you, who you are, the Holy One of God; you have come only to destroy me."
And Christ commanded the earth, and it opened and swallowed that demon, and it went down into the depths of hell.
And then he came to the village whose name was Bethany, where Lazarus had died four days before, and he lay in the tomb.
And Christ went to the door of the tomb, called out and said: "Lazarus, come out!"
And at that single word of Christ he came out of the tomb rejoicing. And the people marvelled, and the people grew all the more in great faith.
After this Christ went up to Jerusalem and entered the temple of God, and he saw a market set up there, and they were selling.
And Christ took a whip and drove those men out, scattered that merchandise, overturned those tables, and said:
"Thus it is written: 'My Father's house shall be called a house of prayer,' but you have made it like a den of robbers."
And then he said: "I will destroy this temple, and on the third day I will build it up."
And when the Jews heard this, they became very angry and said: "We know his father Joseph and his mother Mary, and he has brothers too.
Yet he declares himself the Son of God and claims the temple of God as his ancestral inheritance." And then they said:
"Solomon built it in forty years, and he speaks of destroying it and building it up on the third day."
Because of this saying the Jews set their hearts against him, harboured envy in their hearts, and plotted to seize him and kill him.
And they seized Christ and brought him before the chief priests and the elders, and the chief priests and the elders said to Christ:
"How is it that you declare yourself the Son of God? Are you the Son of God?" But Christ said to them: "You have said so."
And then they said to Christ: "Solomon built this temple in forty years, and you said, 'I will destroy it and in three days I will build it up'!"
Then Christ said: "I have the power to destroy it and to build it up on the third day."
Then the Jews became even angrier; they rose up and stirred up the Jewish people and said: "This man deserves to be put to death."
And they fell upon Christ and began to beat him and mock him.
One struck his head with a [?], one struck his holy head with a reed, one struck him on the cheek, and some spat in his radiant face.
And they set up a cross, crucified Christ, and gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink on the cross.
Then he lifted his eyes to heaven, toward the Father, and said: "My Father, I have accomplished everything, yet Israel did not listen to me, and they have brought such suffering upon me."
And he bowed his head and gave up his spirit. And they quickly took him down from the cross.
Now there was a man of authority who had been a disciple of Christ. He took the body of Christ, laid it in a new tomb, and rolled a great stone against the door of the tomb.
And on the third day, just at the approach of dawn, an angel came down from heaven and rolled the stone away from the tomb.
And Christ rose and came out of the tomb, and he appeared to two disciples, to Mary Magdalene and to other women.
And Christ said to them: "Tell my disciples: Go to Galilee, to Tabor, and there you will see me."
The twelve disciples went with great joy to Mount Tabor. There they saw Christ, worshipped him, and kissed his holy feet.
Christ said to his disciples: "From now on you shall no longer be called disciples; you shall be called apostles.
I am now going up to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God." Then he breathed the living Spirit into the apostles and said to them:
"Receive the Spirit of life. Go to the cities, the countryside and the villages, from one end of the earth to the other, and perform
signs, wonders and healings. Convert the gentiles and baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
Teach them everything I have commanded you. And see, I am with you all the days of your life, until the end of the world.
You received without payment, so give to them without payment." Then Christ ascended into heaven with the angels.
The twelve apostles went out and travelled around the countryside, the cities and the villages. They proclaimed the good news and preached Christ risen from the dead.
They performed signs, wonders and healings, and people were converted and baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
"In this way Christianity multiplied and spread, and it extended from one end of the earth to the other.
They appointed bishops and priests and built churches.
The cross was raised up in them. The whole world believed in Christ, the whole world was filled with Christians, and Christ was preached in every land.
As for the Jews, what the prophets had foretold came upon them:
some died and perished by the sword, some by famine, some by death [plague?], and others were scattered into captivity.
For they did not keep the law of the living God.
Now he has called the Christians Israel, for "Israel" is interpreted as "people of God and servant of Christ." To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
"Then, when I had understood, and had learned everything from Samuel the archdeacon, from the beginning up to now, and had examined the whole law of the Jews and of the Christians,
I came to believe in God who has no beginning, and in his Son Jesus Christ, and in his Holy Spirit.
In this faith I have been baptized, and no one can separate me from Christ until my soul departs. As for the law of my fathers, I am horrified even to speak of it, and ashamed.
For God made heaven and earth; the sun, the moon and the stars; the sea and the dry land; the rivers and the gatherings of the waters; the mountains and the hills; the plains and the forests;
wood and fire; four-footed cattle and wild beasts; creeping things and the birds of the sky. After that God created man and made him lord over all of it.
He made all this subject to man. Shall we then abandon God, the Creator of all this, and call what God created a god? Let it not be!
The sun, the moon and the stars are not gods. God commanded the sun to give light by day, and he commanded the moon and the stars to give light by night, but they are not gods.
God gives a command to the cloud, and it spreads over the brightness of the sun and darkens the moon. For this reason the sun and the moon are not gods.
"Then again, fire is not God, for this reason: a man kindles fire and a man also puts it out. Man is lord over fire, and so fire is not God.
If it gets away from someone and spreads, then wherever it heads, whether into a forest, a field or a house, if it meets a man there, it burns him too.
But when water reaches the fire, it puts out all that great power of the fire, and the fire vanishes. By this it is not God, and yet we believe it to be God.
"Rather, God gave us fire to serve us: for warming ourselves in the cold and for preparing all our food.
When we wish, we kindle it, and when we wish, we put it out. And so that fire is not God.
"Moreover, we men, created by God, used to be like the cattle of the pasture.
In the same way that among cattle the males and females know neither their parent nor their offspring, and so their males and females mate indiscriminately,
so too we, men endowed with speech, were like those cattle: we did not know our own parent or offspring, and we mingled our nature indiscriminately.
But now, by the grace of God, since baptism came about and men came to know the law of Christianity, from that time that lawless practice has been abolished and has vanished.
And this I beg of you, our Lord Jesus Christ: that my body be buried at Mtskheta, where I received baptism at the hand of Catholicos Samuel and was made worthy of the law of the Christians.
From now on no one can separate me from love of you, from faith in you, and from longing for you.
As it is written: neither tortures, nor beatings, nor hunger in prison, nor the sword,
nor the death of this flesh of mine can separate me from you, Lord Jesus Christ."
Then the marzban Buzmir said to him:

"My son Eustathius, listen to me. Do not cut short the days of your life for the sake of Christianity. Do not make your wife a widow and your children orphans, and do not be cut off from your companions in this life."
Saint Eustathius said to him: "Before you, other rulers tortured me severely and beat me, and I did not submit to them. Should I now obey you? Far be that from me!"

Then Buzmir the marzpan saw how firm and unshakable the heart and mind of the blessed Eustathius were. He could not persuade him to return to his ancestral religion, neither by threats and torture nor by promises of good things,
to hold [it] [?]. So he commanded his servants: "Take him to prison, and secretly, at night, cut off his head,
so that none of the Christians may know of it and honour his body. Then carry his flesh outside the city and scatter it, to be eaten by beasts and birds."
The servants led the blessed Eustathius to prison to carry out the marzpan's command.
Saint Eustathius said to them: "Wait for me a little, my brothers, since I am in your hands, so that I may pray to my God."
They agreed to wait a little and gave him time, saying to him: "Let us do so." Then he bent his knees, raised his eyes to heaven and said:
"Lord God, Almighty, you who desire the salvation of all people who hope with faith in your holy name,
you who heard the prayer of the martyrs of old, some of whom perished by the edge of the sword, and some in a lake through freezing,
Some perished by being thrown into the sea, some by fire, and some were devoured by wild beasts for the sake of your name, and they received what you promised,
which eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and which has not entered the heart of man, which you prepared for your holy martyrs.
Make me also worthy, Lord, to be a partaker with them, in the inheritance with them, in the joy with them, in the endless delight with them,
I, the least of the martyrs of the latter times, as the apostle Paul says: "I am the least of the apostles."
You know, my Lord Jesus Christ, that I have preferred no one to you, neither father, nor mother, nor brothers,
nor kinsfolk, but I have loved you alone, the Lord, and for the sake of your name, behold, my head is being cut off today.
And this I pray, and I beseech you, and I ask of you, the Good One, that my body not be left here in Tbilisi,
but that it be buried in holy Mtskheta, where you revealed yourself to me, and that my bones may have grace and healing, as did those former ones."
And he heard a voice which spoke to Eustathius and said: "You will not be less than those former ones who believed in me, in the grace of healing.
And do not be anxious about your body; let it be as you have said it should be." And the blessed Eustathius rejoiced and gave thanks to God.
Saint Eustathius had earlier instructed the blessed Stephen: "When my death becomes known to you, quickly carry my body to Mtskheta and bury it there, where I was baptized."
And when he had finished his prayer, supplication and petition to the Lord, he said to the marzban's servants:
"Now carry out the sentence that has been decreed against me." But they did not want to kill him.
But one of them said: "We will be put to death if he stays alive."
Then they laid their hands on him and struck his venerable neck with a sword and cut off his head, and he commended his soul to Christ the King.
His body they carried outside by night and threw it down there.
But some Christians learned of this and carried it to Mtskheta, for Stephen had instructed the Christians who were there.
When they reached Mtskheta, they told Stephen, and Stephen informed Samuel the catholicos.
He rejoiced greatly and buried him with great glory and honor in the holy church of Mtskheta, and to this day healings of the sick take place by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ,
to whom belong the kingdom and the power, honor and might and unfailing glory, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
